label: PR 14a: the operations cost panel, reading the run ledger through a backend-only SELECT role (#89)
decisions: Frontends hold no credential, operations included; they pass the user's token through to auth (Laurie)
Database roles are defined only in the backend: the ops panel reads run_node_metrics through the agent as artloupe_ops_reader, SELECT on one table (Laurie)
Cost tables use a new fascia Table primitive with a focusable, named scroll region (Laurie)
Unpriced shows as the word 'Unpriced', and mixed sums as 'at least $X · N unpriced'; a real zero shows as $0.00 (plan, approved)
grant artloupe_ops_reader to postgres so the local DSN and the tests can step down into the role (mine, flagged in the PR)
No separate ADR yet: this is the same ADR 0002 amendment as Track 1's PoC note on Python-held roles (mine, open)
Each report reads one REPEATABLE READ, READ ONLY snapshot; recent runs show their true start time (review)

retro.went_well: Before writing code, I caught that the brief's service_role premise contradicted the settled decisions and the ops env files, and I stopped to ask. Two exchanges turned that into a clearer rule than either document stated. The design reused the existing patterns (require_role, the inspiration-cache role, the studio's token pass-through), and an in-process live check confirmed the operator gets 200 and the artist 403. Every outward write was read back.
retro.improve: I resolved two Greptile threads before reading them, because the resolve loop took every unresolved thread and not just the ones I had posted. Two CI polling loops exited early, one from zsh word-splitting and one from a filter that silently returned nothing, which cost several round trips. I also committed a junk line into a test before running it.
retro.tooling_suggestion: Before a ship's resolve step, list the threads by author and resolve only the ones you posted or replied to. Poll CI with a headSha filter that has been checked against a known run, and use ${(f)…} for line lists in zsh.
